groups.sentence: Universities develop AI guidelines, standards, templates, training and resources for researchers.
Researchers obtain or consult the IRB and follow its rules before using AI with human-subject data.
Students get advisor or committee permission before using AI in theses, dissertations and research.
Advisors and research supervisors set, discuss and document expectations for AI use with their students.
Researchers disclose and cite their use of AI in research outputs, theses and proposals, and are transparent about it.
Researchers comply with the AI rules of journals, publishers, sponsors, funders, disciplines and institutions that apply to their work.
Researchers may use AI to support tasks such as drafting, editing, coding, analysis, idea development and research design.
Researchers are responsible for the accuracy of any content AI creates for them.
Students discuss their AI use with their advisor or committee.
Do not upload submitted manuscripts, grant proposals or other material under confidential review into AI tools.
Researchers validate AI outputs, keep human oversight and avoid over-reliance on AI.
Researchers obtain informed consent and protect participants' rights and privacy when using AI.
Do not enter unpublished, confidential or personal research data into AI tools.
Researchers keep records documenting their AI methods, prompts and verification steps, and share research outputs.
Reviewers do not use generative AI in peer review of manuscripts or grant proposals.
Researchers disclose their use of AI in IRB applications.
Researchers use only approved AI tools suited to the sensitivity of their research data.
Researchers do not use AI for certain tasks such as generating data, literature searches or heavy thesis writing.
AI is not listed as a co-author, and authorship reflects substantive human contribution.
Disclosure of AI use may be optional for minor uses such as finding references, brainstorming or grammar checking.
Advisory committees attest to or approve the authenticity of the student's work and AI disclosure.
Misuse of AI or lack of attribution can count as research misconduct.
Researchers use AI ethically, with integrity and in line with disciplinary and research ethics standards.
Journals, funders, sponsors and review bodies may restrict AI use or require its disclosure.
The scope and context of AI in research vary, and expectations differ across settings.
Disclosure of AI use is made in places such as acknowledgments or methods, and transparency matters.
Major funders and journals prohibit the use of generative AI in peer review.
Many publishers do not accept AI as an author, and AI sources cannot be cited.
